content.title: About
content.content: Ranch dressing is a popular creamy sauce made from buttermilk, mayonnaise, herbs and spices (typically garlic, onion, dill, and parsley). It originated in the United States in the 1950s and has become a classic accompaniment for salads, vegetable sticks, chicken wings and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original recipe was created at the Hidden Valley restaurant in California.
Ranch is frequently used as a dip for french fries and chicken nuggets.
In the US more than 30 % of all sold sauces are Ranch.
There are many variations, including bacon, jalapeño, cheddar cheese and more.
In Russia it is sold under brands such as “Ranch”, “Cream Ranch” and similar names.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The creamy base provides calcium, which is important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mayonnaise and buttermilk contribute small amounts of vitamins B2 and B12.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: When buttermilk is used, it may contain live cultures beneficial for gut microbiota.

items.title: Improves vegetable intake
items.content: Ranch makes vegetables more appealing, helping increase their consumption.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Contains fats that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Ranch dressing is rich in fats, so it should be consumed in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Dairy and egg allergy
items.content: Contains milk and eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Commercial versions often contain a lot of salt, which is undesirable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives and artificial additives
items.content: Some store‑bought varieties include emulsifiers and flavor enhancers that may be unwanted for certain consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ranch dressing is served as a sauce for salads, vegetable sticks, french fries, chicken wings and sandwiches. It can be mixed into pasta, pizza, or used as a meat marinate. For a lighter version, blend yogurt with the same herbs instead of mayonnaise.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in a sealed container and use within 2 weeks after opening. At temperatures above +4 °C the product can spoil quickly. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color change, or mold.
